story.title: House Ethics Committee Investigates Max Miller Over Domestic Abuse Allegations
story.summary: The House Ethics Committee has initiated an investigation into Representative Max Miller following domestic abuse allegations made by his ex-wife. Miller has requested the inquiry himself, stating his intention to clear his name and asserting that he has 'absolutely nothing to hide.'

event_overview.title: About New Restraining Order Filed Against GOP Rep. Max Miller Amid Abuse Allegations
event_overview.subject: New Restraining Order Filed Against GOP Rep. Max Miller Amid Abuse Allegations
event_overview.summary: This event concerns a public and legal dispute involving Rep. Max Miller, an Ohio Republican, and his former wife, Emily Moreno, over domestic-abuse allegations, child-custody litigation, and related civil claims. Miller has denied abusing Moreno or their child and has separately sued Moreno and her lawyers for defamation; the allegations had also prompted a House Ethics Committee investigation as of August 5, 2026.

facts.label: People and office
facts.value: Max L. Miller is the Republican U.S. representative for Ohio’s 7th Congressional District; Emily Moreno is his former spouse and the daughter of Ohio Sen. Bernie Moreno.

facts.label: Underlying litigation
facts.value: The dispute has unfolded alongside litigation over custody of Miller and Moreno’s minor child. On May 13, 2026, Miller filed a Cuyahoga County civil defamation case against Moreno and her attorneys, alleging that abuse accusations were false and damaging; the filing identifies the case as CV 26 138810 and seeks damages exceeding $25,000.

facts.label: Relevant Ohio legal framework
facts.value: Ohio Revised Code §3113.31 permits domestic-violence civil-protection-order petitions by qualifying family, household, or dating-relationship parties. It allows same-day ex parte hearings when requested and permits temporary restrictions or other relief when the court finds good cause, but proceedings do not replace other civil or criminal remedies.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the late-July to August 5, 2026 escalation—an attorney-contact restraining-order request, Bernie Moreno’s public criticism, and House Ethics action—but does not resolve the underlying allegations, custody proceedings, or defamation case.

explore_lenses.label: How did this reach the Ethics Committee?
explore_lenses.title: A custody dispute became a House conduct review
explore_lenses.summary: The ethics action follows a prolonged divorce, custody, and civil-litigation fight between Miller and his ex-wife, Emily Moreno. The committee has said it is reviewing allegations involving domestic violence, abuse, and illegal drug use; that statement is not a finding that any allegation is true.

claims.text: The committee said it is reviewing whether Miller may have engaged in domestic violence and abuse or illegal drug use; its public announcement did not establish wrongdoing.

Miller filed a May 2026 defamation lawsuit against Emily Moreno and her attorneys, alleging that their public accusations falsely portrayed him as a violent and abusive father; the lawsuit says allegations made in the custody litigation are unfounded.

Emily Moreno has alleged that Miller scalded, hit, and threatened her during their marriage; Miller has denied those allegations. Their competing accounts also extend to the circumstances of their young daughter's broken collarbone, according to reporting based on court filings and police reports.

explore_lenses.label: Why does an ethics review matter now?
explore_lenses.title: It adds institutional scrutiny during a reelection fight
explore_lenses.summary: The review puts a House oversight body into a matter that had primarily been fought through family-court and civil proceedings. It also arrives on August 5, 2026, the reported deadline for replacing Miller as the Republican candidate in his House race.

claims.text: Miller requested an ethics investigation into himself and said he wanted to clear his name; the committee's announcement did not specify whether his request or another complaint triggered the review.
Sen. Bernie Moreno, Miller's former father-in-law, said Miller should not serve in the House and expressed concern for his daughter and granddaughter; Miller has continued to deny abuse allegations.

AP reported that Miller said he would remain in the reelection race ahead of the Wednesday, August 5, 2026 deadline to replace him on the ballot, while Democrats viewed the contest as more competitive amid the allegations.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next in the House process?
explore_lenses.title: Most investigative work may remain confidential
explore_lenses.summary: A House ethics inquiry can gather documents and witness testimony before the public sees a formal charge or hearing. If an investigative subcommittee is created, it can recommend no action or issue a formal Statement of Alleged Violation, which would begin a separate adjudicatory stage.

claims.text: Under the committee's rules, a member's written request for an investigation of their own conduct is considered under the same rule that permits the committee to review information indicating a possible violation.

If an investigative subcommittee is established, it consists of four members divided equally between the parties and may collect evidence, interview witnesses, and authorize subpoenas by majority vote.

A formal Statement of Alleged Violation requires a finding of substantial reason to believe a violation occurred; at a later public adjudicatory hearing, committee counsel must prove allegations by clear and convincing evidence.

The timing and public visibility of the next steps are uncertain because committee rules generally restrict disclosure of investigative evidence and information unless the committee authorizes release.

story_report.summary: The House Ethics Committee has opened a review of Ohio Republican Rep. Max Miller concerning domestic-abuse allegations raised by his ex-wife, Emily Moreno. The committee said it is examining whether Miller may have engaged in domestic violence and abuse or illegal drug use, while stressing no finding of wrongdoing in its announcement. Miller requested an investigation, saying he wants to clear his name; the review places the disputed accusations before the House’s ethics process.

sections.heading: Miller and Moreno Offer Conflicting Accounts
sections.body: Moreno has alleged that Miller scalded, hit and threatened her during their marriage. Miller has denied the allegations and, in a May defamation lawsuit against Moreno and her attorneys, alleged that public accusations falsely portrayed him as a violent and abusive father. Their accounts also differ over the circumstances of their young daughter’s broken collarbone, according to reporting based on court records and police reports.

sections.heading: Miller Remains in Reelection Race
sections.body: Miller said he would remain in his reelection race before the Aug. 5, 2026, deadline to replace him on the ballot. Sen. Bernie Moreno, his former father-in-law, said Miller should not serve in the House and voiced concern for his daughter and granddaughter, while Miller has continued to deny the abuse allegations. Democrats viewed the contest as more competitive amid the allegations, though the ethics review alone does not determine its electoral effect.

sections.heading: House Ethics Committee Review Process
sections.body: Under House Ethics Committee rules, a member’s written request for an inquiry is considered under the same rule that allows the panel to review information indicating a possible violation. If the committee creates an investigative subcommittee, its four members would be evenly split between the parties and could gather evidence, interview witnesses and authorize subpoenas by majority vote. A formal allegation requires substantial reason to believe a violation occurred, and committee counsel must meet a clear-and-convincing-evidence standard at a later public adjudicatory hearing.

unresolved.text: The committee has not publicly released evidence or conclusions, and it is not known whether it has named an investigative subcommittee, what evidence it will seek or when it will report. Committee rules generally restrict disclosure of investigative information unless the panel authorizes its release.
